Aggregate ringbp outbreak simulations by time interval

Source: R/aggregate.R
aggregate.ringbp.Rd

Aggregates the simulated cases in the $outbreak_ts element of a <ringbp> object (returned by outbreak_model() or scenario_sim()) into the number of new cases, by symptom onset time, in each time interval.

This is called internally by outbreak_model() using the aggregation argument of sim_opts(), and can also be called by users to aggregate simulation output to a different time interval after the simulation.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'ringbp'
aggregate(x, interval, ...)

Arguments

x

a <ringbp> object: the output of outbreak_model() or scenario_sim().

interval

the time interval to aggregate the outbreak simulation to, accepts the same values as the aggregation argument of sim_opts().

...

dots Not used; any extra arguments are ignored with a warning.

Value

A <ringbp> object with the $outbreak_ts element aggregated to interval. The $outbreak_stats element is unchanged. See outbreak_model() for a description of the $outbreak_ts columns for each time interval.

Details

Time in the ringbp model is measured in days since the exposure of the initial cases (day 0); there are no calendar dates. The time intervals are therefore fixed-length blocks of days counted from day 0 (a "weekly" interval is 7 days and a "monthly" interval is 30 days), and are not aligned to calendar weeks or months.

Aggregated output contains every interval from 0 up to the end of the simulation, the final interval ends at cap_max_days (see sim_opts()). Intervals with no cases are included with zero cases. Only cases with symptom onset before cap_max_days are included, as cases with a later symptom onset are not fully simulated.

Aggregation cannot be undone, so a <ringbp> object can only be aggregated if it is disaggregated ("none", i.e. a case line list), or if each new interval is made up of whole intervals of the current aggregation, for example "daily" can be aggregated to "weekly" or "monthly", and "weekly" can be aggregated to 14 (days), but "weekly" cannot be aggregated to "monthly" or "daily". To be able to aggregate to any interval use aggregation = "none" in sim_opts() when running the simulation.

The simulation must also be divided exactly into the new interval, so no simulated cases are dropped and the final interval is complete. For example, a simulation with cap_max_days = 350 can be aggregated from "weekly" to 14 (days), but not to 28 (days) as 350 days is not a whole number of 28 day intervals.

Examples

set.seed(1)
res <- scenario_sim(
  n = 2,
  initial_cases = 1,
  offspring = offspring_opts(
    community = \(n) rnbinom(n = n, mu = 2.5, size = 0.16),
    isolated = \(n) rnbinom(n = n, mu = 0.5, size = 1)
  ),
  delays = delay_opts(
    incubation_period = \(n) rweibull(n = n, shape = 2.32, scale = 6.49),
    onset_to_isolation = \(n) rweibull(n = n, shape = 1.65, scale = 4.28)
  ),
  event_probs = event_prob_opts(
    asymptomatic = 0,
    presymptomatic_transmission = 0.5,
    symptomatic_traced = 0.2
  ),
  interventions = intervention_opts(),
  sim = sim_opts(cap_max_days = 70, aggregation = "none")
)

# case line list
res$outbreak_ts

#>     <int>     <num>      <int>
#>  1:     1  2.305809          1

#>  6:     2  9.306320          4

#> 10:     2 16.083808          8
#> 11:     2 16.261532          9

# aggregate to daily cases
aggregate(res, interval = "daily")

#>        sim   day daily_cases cumulative

# aggregate to fortnightly cases
aggregate(res, interval = 14)
